previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and GERD was admitted for chest pain radiating to the left arm and bilateral flank pain. Initial evaluation revealed an elevated troponin and EKG changes consistent with NSTEMI. She underwent cardiac catheterization, which showed a 90% stenosis in the SVG to RCA graft, successfully treated with two bare metal stents. Her chest pain resolved post-procedure. Blood pressure and diabetes were suboptimal; metoprolol, lisinopril, and simvastatin doses were increased. Her A1c was 11.7%, indicating poor glycemic control, and severe dyslipidemia was noted. She remained stable, with no complications, and was discharged home with medication adjustments and follow-up plans for echocardiography, diabetes management, and orthopedic evaluation for shoulder pain.
